items.caseName: Dargah Hazrat Khalifat-UR Raheman Rehmat-Ulla-Alia (Sunni Malkhed) v. Syeda Ahmedia Banu @ Ahmedunissa Begum & Ors.
items.coram: Justice Manoj Misra and Justice Vijay Bishnoi
items.headline: Supreme Court to examine whether a Mutawalli whose term has ended can carry on Waqf Tribunal proceedings by claiming to be Sajjadanashin
items.text: The Karnataka High Court held that the petitioner was no longer the Mutawalli and could not represent the Dargah, though it let the suit go on through a Waqf Officer appointed by the Board. The Supreme Court framed the question of whether Sajjadanashin status alone is enough to represent the Waqf when there is no Waqfnama, Waqf deed or pleaded custom. The matter is listed for 25 November 2026.

items.caseName: Vipin Kumar Nagar v. Smt. Rakhi Taungar
items.coram: Justice Prakash Padia and Justice Indrajeet Shukla
items.headline: Father's duty to educate a child cannot become a tool of oppression; parents' means must be weighed
items.text: The Division Bench held that under Section 26 of the Hindu Marriage Act a father must educate his child within his means, and that courts must weigh both parents' socio-economic position. Because the child had been studying free at a Central School and the mother moved her to a private school without showing the old school was inadequate, the Court cut the father's monthly liability from Rs 15,000 to Rs 12,000. It added that maintaining the child is a joint duty and that the mother's job does not end the father's obligation.

items.caseName: U.P. Education Service Selection Commissioner, Prayagraj and Another v. Vijay Sonkar and Others
items.coram: Justice Saumitra Dayal Singh and Justice Swarupama Chaturvedi
items.headline: MCQ with more than one correct answer must be dropped or given equal marks; UPTET 2026 results to be revised
items.text: The Division Bench partly allowed the Commission's intra-court appeal over Questions 36 and 37 of UPTET 2026, each of which had two accepted answers. It held that where more than one option is correct the question may be excluded or equal marks given, and that candidates were not barred for failing to object to the provisional key. Unsuccessful candidates get one mark for each of these questions they attempted, already successful candidates are unaffected, and a supplementary result is to be declared, preferably within a month.

items.caseName: Amit Kumar Mishra and 2 Others v. Union of India and 8 Others
items.coram: Justice Chandra Dhari Singh and Justice Tarun Saxena
items.headline: BHU hospital medicine purchase irregularities: High Court calls for enquiry reports, says VC's inaction cannot be ignored
items.text: Hearing a criminal writ PIL that alleges embezzlement in the purchase of medicines, surgical items and equipment for the BHU hospital, the Bench said the Vice-Chancellor's inaction despite several enquiry reports could not be ignored. It directed the Vice-Chancellor or Registrar to file the enquiry reports and any action-taken report within 10 days, and ordered all procurement, tender, stock and payment records preserved. The petitioners want a CBI or SIT probe, and the case is listed on 11 December.

items.coram: Justice Abdul Moin and Justice Pramod Kumar Srivastava
items.headline: High Court stays Gangsters Act FIR and asks UP why such FIRs are still being registered after SC called the law 'stillborn'
items.text: On a writ petition by Brijesh Kumar alias Banty Verma against a Gangsters Act FIR registered on 23 October 2026, the Bench stayed the FIR. It asked why FIRs under the 1986 Act are still being lodged after the Supreme Court described the Act as 'stillborn' in August 2026, and noted that another Division Bench held on 19 November that the Act remains operative. The Additional Chief Secretary (Home) must file a personal affidavit within three weeks, and the case is listed on 15 December.

items.caseName: Sachin Sawant v. Union of India and Another
items.headline: Prior sanction under Section 197 CrPC needed for PMLA prosecution of a public servant; ED complaint against IRS officer quashed
items.text: The High Court quashed the Enforcement Directorate's money-laundering complaint against an IRS officer and the Special Court's cognizance order, because sanction under Section 197(1)(a) CrPC was required and had not been shown. It found that the alleged wealth was accumulated while the officer was performing official duties, and treated the missing sanction as a jurisdictional defect that cannot be cured. The predicate CBI case was not quashed.

items.caseName: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pallavi Arjun Dalvi and Ors.
items.headline: Where claimant and employer are close relatives, Commissioner must call at least one independent witness to prove employment
items.text: The Aurangabad Bench held that Commissioners under the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923 must examine at least one independent witness, besides the claimant and the employer-relative, before finding an employer-employee relationship between close relatives. It set aside a Rs 6,55,840 award to the widow and minor child of a tractor driver said to be employed by his father, and sent the matter back for fresh evidence. The Labour Court must finish the trial within three months.

items.caseName: Rupesh Kumar Jha v. Central Consumer Protection Authority & Ors.
items.headline: A complaint filed by one consumer is not by itself an 'individual' grievance; CCPA closure of CUET-UG books complaint set aside
items.text: The High Court set aside a CCPA communication that closed a complaint about CUET (UG) 2025 books as an individual grievance. It held that the fact that one consumer filed the complaint does not make the grievance individual, and that the communication gave no reasons and ignored the nationwide scope of the exam and its marketing. The CCPA must pass a reasoned order within two months.

items.caseName: Srimanta Das and 42 Ors. v. The State of Assam and 15 Ors.
items.headline: Special Police Officers cannot claim re-induction once the situation that required them has normalised
items.text: Forty-three former Home Guards and SPOs from the Bodoland Territorial Council area challenged their discharge and the refusal to re-engage or regularise them. The High Court held that the SPO post is not permanent under the statute, so re-induction cannot be claimed once the situation has normalised. It directed that their candidature in the Constable recruitment be considered on par with similarly placed persons, giving weight to their experience.

items.caseName: United India Insurance Company Ltd v. Md Amsher Ali & Ors.
items.headline: Farm labourer riding in trailer to load and unload produce is not a gratuitous passenger; insurers liable
items.text: The High Court held that an agricultural labourer travelling in a trailer to load and unload farm produce is linked to the trailer's agricultural use and is not a gratuitous passenger under an agricultural liability policy. It dismissed the insurer's appeal and upheld compensation of Rs 5,30,000 with 6% interest. Both insurers are to pay equally.

items.caseName: Smti Renu Dangoria v. The State of Assam and 5 Ors
items.headline: Site plan by an architect cannot replace the engineer certification a liquor shop tender expressly requires
items.text: The High Court dismissed a writ petition against the rejection of a liquor shop bidder's technical bid, which lacked the engineer-certified site plan required by the tender checklist. It held that the tender must be read as a whole and that the petitioner did not meet a stated eligibility condition, so Article 14 gave no ground to interfere. The alleged upload irregularity by the successful bidder was found not to be a substantive defect.

items.coram: Justice Michael Zothankhuma and Justice Sanjeev Kumar Sharma
items.headline: Social media post showing wife enjoying life does not prove she can maintain herself
items.text: The Division Bench set aside the Nalbari Family Court's refusal of maintenance and ordered the husband to pay Rs 2,000 a month from November 2026. It held that a social media post showing the wife's 'enjoyable life' in Guwahati did not show that she could fund that lifestyle from her own work. Finding her only partly able to support herself, the Court awarded extra support so she could keep her pre-separation standard of living.

items.caseName: State of Gujarat v. Pravinbhai @ Lalo Sandhabhai Prajapati
items.coram: Justice Bhargav D. Karia and Justice Hemant M. Prachchhak
items.headline: 28 years on, High Court upholds acquittal in POCSO case over faulty test identification parade
items.text: The Division Bench dismissed the State's appeal and upheld the trial court's acquittal. It found that identity was not proved beyond reasonable doubt because the investigating officer and the Executive Magistrate did not follow proper procedure in the test identification parade. It also relied on the delayed FIR, the victim's earlier statements to doctors that her injuries came from a fall, and gaps in the serological evidence.

items.caseName: Shiva Kumar Deora @ Shiva Ratan Deora v. Union of India, through Directorate of Enforcement
items.headline: Delay in trial alone cannot override PMLA bail conditions; bail refused to alleged mastermind of Rs 750 crore fake ITC racket
items.text: The High Court dismissed the renewed bail plea of a man accused of running a syndicate of 135 shell companies that generated about Rs 750 crore in fraudulent input tax credit. It held that about 18 months in custody, or delay in trial, does not on its own satisfy Section 45 PMLA, and that the gravity and social impact of the offence must also be weighed. It rejected his claim to parity with a co-accused and found that his medical conditions could be managed in jail.

items.headline: KPSC recruitment scam: High Court calls ED disclosures 'shocking', orders FIRs to be registered and sent to SIT
items.text: In a Saturday sitting, the High Court directed that information shared by the Enforcement Directorate under Section 66(2) of the PMLA be registered as cognisable offences through the jurisdictional police, including Vidhana Soudha Police Station, and then transferred to the SIT without delay. The case concerns alleged irregularities in KPSC recruitment to 50 Industrial Extension Officer posts and 400 Veterinary Officer posts.
items.why: Opens the way for criminal cases based on ED material in a major state recruitment scandal.

items.caseName: Ms. Chanda Kochhar v. Sri Dinabandhu Dash & Ors
items.headline: High Court quashes 2013 cognizance against Chanda Kochhar over alleged illegal deductions from a customer's ICICI account
items.text: The High Court set aside the Bhubaneswar SDJM's cognizance order of 9 January 2013 on a complaint that an account was opened fraudulently and money deducted without authority. It held that, even taking the complaint and witness statements at face value, no offence under the IPC sections invoked was made out, and that the magistrate had not applied his mind. The complainant did not appear despite notice.

items.caseName: Amal Raj v. State of Bihar and Anr.
items.headline: Being a school principal does not by itself attract liability under Section 19 POCSO without knowledge of the offence
items.text: The High Court held that liability under Sections 19 and 21 of the POCSO Act requires proof that the person knew or suspected an offence and failed to report it, not merely that they held the post of principal. Finding no material showing abetment or culpable omission by the principal in a case where two sports teachers allegedly harassed a student, it quashed the 4 February 2025 cognizance order and POCSO Case No. 30 of 2024 against him.
